caption:
OpusClip turns one long video into short clips for Reels, TikTok and Shorts.
Paste a YouTube link or upload a file, pick a clip model, and it finds the moments for you.
The free plan gives 60 credits a month, and 1 credit is 1 minute of your original video.

What long video would you cut into shorts first?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: OpusClip Help Center · Photo: OpusClip
threads_text: OpusClip cuts a long video into short clips on its own, and you can tell it what to find in plain words. The free plan is 60 credits a month, and each credit is one minute of the original video. Would you trust an AI to pick your best moments?

slides.headline: How to use *Opus Clip* to turn long videos into shorts

slides.heading: 1. *Add* your video
paras: Paste a video link or upload a file.
The free plan takes YouTube links and local files. Videos can run up to 10 hours.

slides.heading: 2. Tell it *what to find*
paras: Pick ClipAnything as the clip model, then type a prompt in plain English.
Example: "Find the moments most likely to go viral on social media."

slides.heading: 3. Pick a *caption style*
paras: Choose one of the Quick Presets for captions.
Pick No Caption if your video already has subtitles.

slides.heading: 4. Watch the *credits*
paras: 1 credit is 1 minute of the original video, not per clip. A 30 minute video costs 30.
Free: 60 credits a month, with a watermark.

slides.hook: Follow for one AI tool explained every day.

site_article.headline: How to use Opus Clip for free: turn long videos into shorts
site_article.dek: OpusClip finds the best moments in a long video and cuts them into vertical clips. Here is how to make your first clips, write prompts that work and make the free credits last.
site_article.summary: OpusClip is a tool that turns long videos into short clips for social media. The free plan gives 60 credits a month, and each credit covers one minute of the original video.
site_article.seo_title: How to use Opus Clip for free: long videos into shorts
site_article.seo_description: How to use Opus Clip: add a video, pick ClipAnything, write prompts that find the right moments, choose captions and make 60 free credits last.
site_article.answer_summary: To use Opus Clip, paste a YouTube link or upload a video, choose a clip model such as ClipAnything, optionally type a prompt for the moments you want, pick a caption style and generate. Processing costs 1 credit per minute of the original video, and the free plan gives 60 credits a month.

paragraphs.text: How to use Opus Clip, in short: give it a long video, tell it what kind of moments you want, and it cuts them into short clips with captions, ready for Reels, TikTok or YouTube Shorts. OpusClip describes itself as a clipping tool that turns long videos into shorts and can publish them to social platforms.

You can start for free. The free plan gives 60 credits a month, adds an OpusClip watermark to your clips, and takes YouTube links and local files as sources. Paid plans start with Starter at $15 a month for 150 credits, and Pro at $29 a month, according to the pricing page.
How Opus Clip credits work

This is the part people miss. Credits are charged per minute of the original video you import, not per clip you get back. A 30 minute podcast costs 30 credits whether it produces 5 clips or 20. Partial minutes round down, so a 4.5 minute video counts as 4, but anything under a minute still costs 1 credit.

On monthly plans, credits expire after 60 days, so unused credits roll over for one extra month. Yearly plans get the full year of credits up front. On the free plan, the pricing page says clips can no longer be exported after 3 days, so download what you want soon after it is made.
Use the Processing timeframe slider to process only the part of the video you care about. A 90 minute stream where only the last 20 minutes matter then costs 20 credits instead of 90.
How to make your first clips in Opus Clip

paragraphs.title: 1. Add your video
paragraphs.text: Sign in and paste a video link or upload a file. Free accounts can use YouTube links and local files. Starter adds Google Drive, Vimeo, Zoom, Rumble and StreamYard. OpusClip says it supports videos up to 10 hours long.

paragraphs.title: 2. Choose the clip model
paragraphs.text: Under Clip model, select ClipAnything. OpusClip says it finds moments using visual, audio and sentiment cues, and recommends it for videos with little or no talking, like sports, gaming or vlogs. For interviews and podcasts, the talking is what matters.

paragraphs.title: 3. Pick a genre and set the options
paragraphs.text: Selecting your video genre is optional. Set the clip length here too: by default it is Auto, which means clips of up to 3 minutes. Prompts cannot change clip length, so set it in this box.

paragraphs.title: 4. Type a prompt (optional)
paragraphs.text: Write what you want in plain English. A good prompt names the subject, the action and the feeling or sound you are looking for. The examples below come from OpusClip's own prompt manual.

paragraphs.title: Prompt 1: The safe default
paragraphs.text: Find the moments most likely to go viral on social media

paragraphs.title: Prompt 2: For podcasts and interviews
paragraphs.text: Show me moments with strong opinions or words

paragraphs.title: Prompt 3: For product videos
paragraphs.text: Show me the host unboxing a new tech gadget and explaining its features

paragraphs.title: Prompt 4: For a compilation
paragraphs.text: Find all the scenes with laughter

paragraphs.title: 5. Pick a caption style
paragraphs.text: Choose a style from Quick Presets, or select No Caption if your video already has subtitles or you want a clean look. Save your favorite model, genre and preset as defaults so you do not set them every time.

paragraphs.title: 6. Review, rate and edit
paragraphs.text: Each clip gets a virality score, the tool's guess of how likely it is to do well. You can sort clips by score or by the order they appear in the video. Use the heart or thumbs down on each clip: disliked clips are hidden. Then open a clip in the editor to trim it, fix captions or change the layout.

paragraphs.title: 7. Download or schedule
paragraphs.text: Download the clip, or connect your social accounts and schedule it. Pro users can also export XML files to keep editing in Adobe Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve.
What prompts cannot do

OpusClip's manual is clear about the limits. Prompts find moments, they do not edit them. A prompt cannot clean up audio, change the aspect ratio, add emojis or transitions, or set clip length. Vague prompts like "Create videos" or "Do it" do not work, and prompts should be written in English. The manual also says it works better to describe what you want than what you do not want.
Be specific about what is on screen. "The woman in the yellow dress" or "audience cheering" gives the model something it can actually look and listen for.
What the free plan is good for

For trying the tool out, it works. A CNET writer who tested the free plan said a video of just over two minutes took about five minutes to process, and one clip scored 85 percent for virality. The same test pointed out the downsides: free clips carry the OpusClip watermark and the credits run out quickly.

The honest math: 60 free credits is one hour of source video a month. That is one podcast episode or a few short streams. If you post clips every day, you will hit the limit in the first week, and the watermark makes free clips look like free clips. Start with your best long video, use the timeframe slider, and only pay once you know the clips actually perform for your account.
The virality score is a guess, not a promise. Watch every clip before you post it. A clip that starts mid sentence or cuts off the punch line will flop no matter what score it got.
